transcript:
Header: 2025-12-04 | 15:30 UTC | Duration: 54 mins
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Jane Thompson (CTO - Omega), Luis Garcia (Head Infra), Priya Menon (Compliance), Arun Bhat (ML Eng)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um quick round of intros, i'm maya from redwood i'm the ae on this account
[00:07] Jane: hi maya jane here cto at omega, thanks for doing this call
[00:11] Luis: luis infra, we'll focus on how this would run in our secure datacenter
[00:14] Priya: priya compliance, hi
[00:16] Daniel: daniel from redwood se, i'll jump in on the technicals
[00:20] Maya: cool, goal today is to understand your constraints for an on-prem air-gapped deployment and see where redwood fits - hosted/dedicated options ruled out by policy?
[00:31] Jane: yea we evaluated hosted briefly but for regulated workflows we need full air-gap, no egress. also procurement prefers a single-vendor on-prem offering if possible
[00:39] Arun: to add, some models run on customer data that cannot leave premises, and the legal team flagged the need for HSM-wrapped keys
[00:47] Daniel: ok makes sense. can you share current infra? what hardware do you have and what's your procurement cadence?
[00:54] Luis: we have a few racks with a mix, older 40GB A100s and a couple of new H100s on order but procurement lead time is 10-12 weeks. budget is tight so we might not get H100s for initial POC
[01:08] Maya: understood. an important part of our private offering is the on-prem package that supports air-gapped installs - offline bundles, installer images and signed artifacts. we also support kms/hsm integrations, can you say which vendor?
[01:24] Priya: we use HashiCorp Vault today, and our security team wants HSM for root keys. we also need SSO via SAML and RBAC controls mapped to AD groups
[01:34] Daniel: we have integrations for Vault and can work with external HSMs, we also support SAML and LDAP for RBAC. the air-gap updates are shipped as signed artifacts and we provide a verification tool to run offline. there is some manual step to pull the update media into the isolated network which your infra team controls
[01:51] Luis: how do we handle model updates? we can't have the model download from internet, so we'd have to stage them offline as well
[01:56] Daniel: yes, model artifacts are treated as signed blobs. for air-gapped sites we provide a transfer bundle. you can host models on local object storage. for large models we recommend quantized variants to reduce size - we can also run updates as incremental KV cache patches to reduce transfer size
[02:14] Jane: that last bit - kv cache patches - can you explain? we've not done that pattern before
[02:18] Daniel: sure, so for transformer models we maintain a key-value cache for recent tokens. for some workloads, rather than shipping whole new weights, we can ship smaller delta bundles for tokenizer/vocab changes or prompts, but full model weight updates will still be required for major model version changes
[02:33] Arun: hmm we typically update models quarterly and anything that requires a full weights update has to go through change control - procurement wants to avoid frequent big downloads
[02:41] Maya: that aligns - we can recommend a POC model and a quantization profile to keep weights small; also describe fallback policies if an update is delayed
[02:50] Priya: also need audit logs and retention policy - can logs be exported to our SIEM?
[02:55] Daniel: yes audit logs are available, we can stream them to your on-prem SIEM via secure channels; logs include per-request metadata, model version, latency and token counts. we can also redact prompts server-side if needed
[03:10] Luis: latency is critical - real-time credit decisioning needs <120ms p95 for short prompts, can redwood meet that on A100s?
[03:20] Daniel: depends on model size and batching. with a quantized 13B variant and properly tuned batching and KV cache warm, hitting ~70-100ms p95 is realistic on A100 40GB for single-request latency, but concurrency and burst patterns will change numbers. H100s would be better but more expensive
[03:40] Jane: what's the tradeoff on quality for quantization? we can't accept major regressions in scoring or hallucinations
[03:46] Daniel: we run quantization-aware evals and can recommend profiles that maintain quality for your eval prompt set; as part of POC we do regression checks against your prompts and provide rollback paths to float weights if needed
[03:59] Maya: of course we also offer canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a hosted-safe variant in non-airgapped configs, but in a strict air-gap that's not possible so we need robust rollback processes and offline signed backups
[04:12] Priya: one more thing - encryption at rest and KMS integration. Vault meets our key rotation requirements?
[04:18] Daniel: we support external KMS including Vault; keys can be wrapped in HSM and we support periodic rotation. we also have options for encrypted local disk volumes and object storage integration with server-side encryption
[04:33] Speaker 1: okay great, how about licensing and support SLAs for private installs
[04:36] Maya: for private we do platform license + optional support tiers, dedicated reserved capacity is separate product. SLAs can be negotiated for on-call support, and we offer upgrade windows for air-gapped maintenance. i'll share the pricing template after this call
[04:49] Luis: procurement will need a clear list of deliverables for the on-prem handoff - what does the install require?
[04:56] Daniel: we provide an install runbook, preflight checker for the target hosts, container images, and an offline install bundle. for restricted installs we can do remote screen-share-assisted installs but not remote network access. we also supply a verification script to validate signatures
[05:12] Arun: what about model onboarding - will redwood help convert our finetuned weights and optimize for quantization?
[05:19] Daniel: yes we offer model onboarding services as part of POC: conversion, quantization, perf tuning, and an eval report. we typically run benchmarks on your hardware or a close proxy and share latency/cost estimates
[05:31] Jane: whats the timeline to get a POC up? procurement lead time on hardware is a blocker
[05:36] Maya: we can run a remote benchmark first against a cloud-hosted dedicated cluster to validate the model and quantization profile while you finish procurement. then when hardware arrives we run the on-prem install and final benchmarks
[05:50] Priya: legal review will need SOC2 evidence and an incident response plan. can you provide templates?
[05:56] Maya: yes, i'll attach our security whitepaper, SOC2 summary, and a sample incident response playbook.
[06:02] Luis: ok next steps?
[06:05] Maya: recap - i'll send security docs and pricing, daniel will send hardware spec, arun to share model sizes and concurrency, and we'll schedule pilot kickoff once procurement timeline is clearer. thanks all
[06:18] Jane: thanks everyone
[06:20] Luis: thanks
[06:22] Priya: bye

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings, speaker labels may be inconsistent. references to KV cache and HSM might be transcribed or abbreviated. Customer emphasized air-gap and procurement lead times.
